source_title: NCS launches AI Mission Centre, commits to building a workforce of more than 300 Forward-Deployed Engineers in the next two years - PR Newswire
source_excerpt:
Commits to growing the current pool of 100 Intelligentisation Forward-Deployed Engineers (iFDEs) to over 300 in the next two years through internal reskilling and external hiring.
NCS AI Mission Centre supports the acceleration of AI adoption across key industries in Singapore.
Announces three strategic AI deploymentÂ MOUs with Changi Airport Group (CAG), the Institute of Mental Health (IMH), and Life3 Biotech. Â
SINGAPORE , Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- NCS today launched theÂ NCS AI Mission Centre, a dedicated innovation and execution hub to help public and private organisations move from AI experimentation to full-scale enterprise deployment. To drive this initiative, NCS is committed to building a workforce of more than 300 Intelligentisation Forward-Deployed Engineers (iFDEs) within the next two years , comprising reskilled internal talent and new hires. iFDEs are domain-expert, vendor-agnostic AI specialists embedded directly within client teams to deliver real-world deployment across key sectors.
NCS also announced three strategic Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) with key industry partners, Changi Airport Group (CAG), the Institute of Mental Health (IMH), and Life3 Biotech to jointly develop and scale innovative AI-driven solutions.
Officiated by Guest-of-Honour Mrs. Josephine Teo, Minister for Digital Development and Information , the AI Mission Centre anchors NCS' commitment to supporting the acceleration of AI adoption across key sectors in Singapore.
NCS CEO Sam Liew said, "We want Singapore to be a place where the world comes to see AI working at scale - strengthening industries, improving public services, and opening new possibilities for our people. The NCS AI Mission Centre is our commitment to that ambition. By growing our current team of 100 iFDEs to more than 300, we are investing in our greatest asset - our people - who can turn technological breakthroughs into everyday progress. Our goal is to build AI capabilities that serve Singapore, and solutions that can make an impact around the world."
Bringing together industry specialists, iFDEs, and AI platform teams, and drawing on NCS' Sunshine.AI suite of products and platforms, the AI Mission Centre will help clients define priority problems, redesign workflows, and test and deploy AI solutions securely in live operations. It will also turn successful deployments into reusable products and capabilities, enabling proven solutions to scale across organisations and markets.
For instance, NCS' Sunshine.core provides a sovereign-ready foundation for building, operating, and governing enterprise AI agents, while Sunshine.commanderAI enables robots from different manufacturers to work together on real-world tasks. Alongside the iFDEs, teams of NCS AI Natives, referred to as "speedboats", support client missions by moving fast and experimenting boldly to deliver innovation at speed. Together, these platforms and teams support the secure integration of AI into clients' digital workflows and physical operations.
Accelerating enterprise AI adoption through strategic MOUs To mark the launch, NCS also signed three strategic MOUs aimed at translating AI concepts into operational outcomes across the Transport, Healthcare, and Advanced Manufacturing industries. While anchored in these initial use cases, the collaborations reflect a broader commitment to accelerating AI adoption and diffusion across the wider economy:
Changi Airport Group (CAG): A partnership to enhance and scale iFerretâ¢ , a co-developed intelligent runway surveillance system that monitors for Foreign Object Debris (FOD), with advanced AI technologies.Â The unique co-innovation model allows operational requirements to be developed and tested in real-world airport environments before global deployment. Â
Institute of Mental Health (IMH): A partnership that combines IMH's clinical expertise and NCS' technology capabilities to explore and co-develop digital solutions that enhance patient care and support healthcare workers in care delivery. One of the first initiatives under this collaboration is Bio-ID , an AI-powered facial recognition solution to strengthen patient identification and support timely awareness of safety considerations in inpatient care settings. IMH will validate the solution in its wards and provide insights in refining the technology for broader deployment across other healthcare and care environments.
Life3 Biotech: A partnership to co-develop AI-driven biomanufacturing optimisation capabilities, integrating AI and advanced bioprocessing technologies. The collaboration aims to enhance production efficiency, scalability, and sustainability of micro-organisms while laying the foundation for next-generation intelligent biomanufacturing infrastructure.
Supporting the development of Singapore's AI talent pipeline NCS is driving extensive people initiatives to build its own iFDE workforce and to help advance the national AI workforce development:
Workforce-wide upskilling: AI fluency training is provided to all NCS employees, including courses on prompt engineering, responsible AI, and collaborating with AI agents to boost productivity. Additionally, over 2,000 AI practitioners are continuously upskilled with advanced AI skills in building and deploying production-ready agentic solutions.
Job redesign initiatives: NCS is redesigning software engineering roles to bring together business analysis, software development, and testing capabilities within more versatile, AI-enabled teams to accelerate time-to-value for clients.

NCS is a leading AI technology services company. With a 15,000-strong team across the Asia Pacific, NCS scales its platforms and capabilities to provide clients with greater agility and AI expertise across a range of Industries. Embracing a strong ecosystem of global partners, NCS transforms technology services delivery combining AI with digital resilience to drive real business impact.
